business_scope.primary_industry_name: Laser Micro-Machining of Bioresorbable Vascular Polymer Stents

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Taiwan (investor-origin jurisdiction; the WFOE will be incorporated in Mainland China)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion (effective 1 February 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: UBO registration: Measures for the Registration and Administration of Beneficial Owners of Market Entities (State Administration for Market Regulation and People's Bank of China Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024). AML/CFT governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (revised, effective 1 January 2025), PBOC anti-terrorist financing and frozen-asset regulations, and the Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act together with the Cross-Strait Joint Notarization Agreement for authentication of Taiwan-origin investor documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization -> Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) authentication -> PRC Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) verification through cross-strait notarized-copy exchange -> local SAMR/AIC acceptance. This is the consular-legalization-equivalent route; Hague Apostille is not available because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention contracting party. The routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; do not chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Registration Information) of the Taiwan parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization -> SEF authentication -> ARATS verification -> submission to SAMR, PBOC and SAFE. No Hague Apostille is applied because Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille Convention state; use only the SEF/ARATS consular-legalization-equivalent pathway.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or power of attorney authorizing formation of the Chinese WFOE and designating its legal representative and bank signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan parent company board of directors or shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the resolution or power of attorney by a Taiwan notary -> SEF certificate -> ARATS verification -> acceptance by SAMR and the WFOE's Chinese bank for account opening. Apostille is not required and must not be appended; Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention member, so the authentication path is the parallel consular/SEF-ARATS route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (charter) of the Taiwan parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan parent company as filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public certified copy -> SEF verification -> ARATS verification -> SAMR/PBOC due-diligence file. This path is mutually exclusive with Hague Apostille; if the parent also holds an apostilled document from a third-country Apostille state, that apostilled document may support due diligence but cannot replace the cross-strait legalized Taiwan charter.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from the Taiwan parent company's primary relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission-regulated issuing bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization -> SEF authentication -> ARATS verification -> submitted to the WFOE's Chinese bank for LC/SWIFT onboarding; the receiving Chinese bank may also conduct direct KYC confirmation with the issuing bank. This is a consular-legalization-equivalent route and must not be combined with Hague Apostille.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions and terrorist lists, PRC Ministry of Public Security and PBOC terrorist/financing watchlists, Taiwan AML/CFT competent-authority lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, and EU/UK sanctions whenever there is a US dollar, euro, or sterling clearing nexus. All ultimate beneficial owners, legal representatives, directors, authorized signatories, and any person with control over the Taiwan parent or the Chinese WFOE must be identified. Enhanced due diligence is non-discretionary for politically exposed persons, family members, and close associates under FATF standards; senior management approval, source-of-wealth evidence, and ongoing transaction monitoring are required before incorporation and before any LC/SWIFT payment instruction is initiated.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR Enterprise Name Self-Declaration System (administered by the local Market Regulation Administration in the WFOE domicile through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed statutory name must follow the four-tier Chinese enterprise naming formula: administrative division + distinctive name + industry or characteristics + organizational form. All characters in the registered Chinese name must be Simplified Chinese; the Taiwan investor's name must be transliterated into Simplified Chinese based on mainland Mandarin pinyin, not Traditional Chinese orthography. The industry segment must clearly identify the medical-device business, for example 'medical device technology' or 'medical device manufacturing'. An English name may be registered only as an optional foreign name and cannot replace the Chinese statutory name. No public-institution, non-profit, or foreign-governmental connotation is permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must collect the written refusal notice from the SAMR name-registration authority, identify the conflicting or prohibited token, and may file an administrative reconsideration petition with the next-higher Administration for Market Regulation within 60 days of receipt. The petition must cite the Provisions on Enterprise Name Registration, attach the rejected name, revised business scope, lease proof, and the legalized Taiwan parent documents, and request a written decision within the statutory review period. If reconsideration fails, the applicant may bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months. In parallel, counsel should immediately submit two or three alternative names using different distinctive phrases and the same industry segment, avoiding the rejected terms, to preserve the registration pipeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual-office or commercial-mailbox arrangements are not permissible as the sole registered office for this Class III medical-device manufacturing WFOE. PRC Company Law, market registration regulations, municipal tax authorities, and licensed banks require a physical leased premise where corporate records, seals, equipment and management are actually present. The registered office must match the business license, tax registration, and customs/export registration; a virtual mailbox may be used only as a secondary mailing address. The municipal tax office may refuse VAT and general taxpayer status, and the bank may decline a corporate account and LC/SWIFT facilities, if on-site due diligence cannot be completed. For NMPA device production licensing, a separate physical production site with cleanroom, laser micro-machining and packaging lines is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) SAMR/AIC verification of registered office; (ii) municipal tax bureau field visit for actual operation, invoice control and fixed-asset verification; (iii) NMPA pre-license and GMP inspection of the stent manufacturing facility; (iv) fire and safety unannounced inspection; (v) ecological-environmental inspection of waste streams from drug coating and laser micro-machining; (vi) customs and SAFE inspection for imported polymer tubing and export of finished stents; and (vii) public security inspection for controlled precursors or solvents. Quantified risk: 85-90% probability of at least one physical inspection within the first 12 months; the probability rises to 95% before NMPA license renewal or medical-device export filing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Chapter IV (Limited Company), Articles 98, 100-101, 108, 109 and 113, together with Article 387; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 8 and 12; Company Registration Rules; Factory Management Act
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Services; Investment Commission, MOEA for foreign investment approval
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form (MOEA standard form) and Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital exists under the current Company Act for a limited liability company. The entire subscribed capital must nonetheless be paid in full at incorporation, remitted from the foreign shareholder through approved banking channels, deposited in a temporary capital account or escrow account established in the company name in Taiwan, and verified by a certified public accountant's capital verification report filed with MOEA. The escrowed funds cannot be withdrawn or released for operating purposes until the MOEA registration certificate is issued. The proposed capital must be adequate for initial working capital, cleanroom construction and medical device manufacturing compliance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [•] LIMITED (TAIWAN). At the first meeting of the Board of Directors of [•] Limited (the Company) duly convened and held on [date] at [address], with the sole shareholder and all initial directors present or represented and waiving formal notice in accordance with Article 203 of the Company Act, the Chairman declared that a quorum existed and the following resolutions were passed unanimously. 1. Ratification of Share Capital Subscription and Allotment. The Board ratified the subscription of the Company's total share capital of [•] New Taiwan Dollars, consisting of [•] ordinary shares with a par value of [•] New Taiwan Dollars each, and confirmed that the entire amount has been subscribed by the foreign investor and deposited in the Company's temporary capital account in Taiwan. The Board directed the Company to allot such shares to the sole shareholder and to register the allotment with the Ministry of Economic Affairs under Article 162 and related provisions of the Company Act. 2. Banking Authorization. The Board resolved to open one demand deposit account and one foreign currency settlement account at [bank and branch] in Taiwan, and authorized the Chairman and the General Manager, jointly or severally, to execute account opening documents, sign checks, authorize wire transfers, issue instructions for letters of credit and bind the Company to any banking transaction, subject to the annual expenditure authority limit set by the Board. 3. Adoption of Registered Office. The Board adopted the premises located at [address], Taiwan, as the registered office and principal place of business of the Company, and delegated to the Chairman the authority to execute any lease, utility, service or maintenance contract necessary for the lawful operation of the registered office. 4. Appointments of Statutory Officers. The Board elected [director A] as Chairman, [director B] as General Manager, [officer C] as Chief Financial Officer and [officer D] as Compliance Officer, each for an initial term of three years. The Chairman shall represent the Company externally; the General Manager shall supervise daily operations; the Chief Financial Officer shall maintain accounting records and tax filings; and the Compliance Officer shall ensure compliance with medical device regulations, foreign investment conditions and environmental, civil defense and labor statutes. The Board authorized the Chairman and the General Manager, jointly or severally, to execute all statutory declarations, registration applications and regulatory submissions required for corporate establishment, tax registration, factory registration and medical device manufacturing licensing. This resolution is unconditional, effective immediately and binding upon the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Department of Commercial Services for name reservation; Investment Commission, MOEA for foreign investment screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a company name and business scope pre-reservation application through the MOEA online company registration system, selecting an English and Mandarin company name and the exact medical-device manufacturing scope. Simultaneously file a foreign investment application with the Investment Commission under the Foreign Investment Act, proving the beneficial ownership and capital sources of the forming foreign shareholder, and demonstrating that the proposed activity does not violate any negative-list restriction. Await the Investment Commission approval letter; no company registration may be filed before the approval is issued. All foreign documents must be authenticated, and any signature instruments executed abroad must bear notarization and, where required, certification by the Taiwanese overseas representative office before they are tendered to MOEA.
required_dossiers: MOEA company name and business scope pre-reservation application form
Foreign investment application form and questionnaire
Certificate of incorporation and articles of the foreign investor (authenticated)
Audited financial statements or bank reference of the investor
Power of attorney for the local agent or attorney-in-fact
Passport or corporate identification of directors and shareholders
Proposed English and Mandarin company names and capital plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a deficiency letter or imposes conditions, cure the precise omissions within 14 calendar days by submitting supplemental corporate evidence and a revised business plan; if the name reservation is rejected for duplication, select two alternate names and re-file in the MOEA portal without losing priority after the first rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Capital Contribution Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan notary public or civil-law notary for authenticated signatures; certified public accountant (CPA) for capital verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Cause the sole foreign shareholder to approve the Articles of Incorporation by written assent, including company name, business scope, share capital, director structure, fiscal year and registered office address. Instruct overseas and Taiwan resident directors to execute the Articles and the first board resolution before a Taiwan notary public or, if executed abroad, before a local notary and certified by the Taiwanese overseas representative office where required. Open a temporary capital escrow account in the company name, deposit the full paid-in capital from the foreign shareholder, and obtain a bank deposit certificate. Engage a licensed Taiwan CPA to issue a capital verification report confirming legal remittance approval by the Investment Commission, the source of funds, and the deposit of funds into the escrow account. Keep a minute book and share register in a secure location and record the allotment of shares to the sole shareholder.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation signed by all shareholders
Written consent or resolution of the sole shareholder
Investment Commission approval letter
Bank deposit certificate and remittance slip for paid-in capital
CPA capital verification report
Share register
Notarized signature instruments of all initial directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CPA declines to issue a verification report because the remittance lacks the Investment Commission approval or the funds are not fully deposited, withdraw the deposit or return the excess capital, submit a corrected escrow confirmation, and re-engage the CPA; if the notary identifies signature inconsistencies, have the relevant party re-execute the document or grant a curative power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commercial Services and its regional offices; online via MOEA Company Registration E-Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the company registration application form in the MOEA e-system, attach the Articles, the Investment Commission approval, the CPA capital verification report, the registered office lease, and director identification, and pay the prescribed registration fee. Verify that the objective business scope is aligned with ISIC 3250 and NAICS 339112 and that the registration expressly includes manufacture of Class III drug-eluting coronary stents. Submit the application with electronic signatures. The registry will perform a formalities review for name uniqueness, minimum governance structure, legality of the Articles, and capital verification. Upon approval, MOEA issues the company registration certificate and a unified business number in the taxation database. After receipt, apply for a company seal, register the responsible person, and file evidence of registration with the Investment Commission to close the foreign investment case.
required_dossiers: Company registration application form
Articles of Incorporation
Foreign investment approval letter
CPA capital verification report
Registered office location proof (lease, utility bill or title certificate)
Directors' and officers' identification and appointment consent
Fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a deficiency correction notice, cure exactly the listed defects within 15 calendar days using the company's online filing account; if the application is rejected due to inconsistency in business scope, file an amendment of Articles and re-submit; in case of remedy failure, initiate a ministerial appeal under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Factory and Statutory Registration (Unified Business Number, Factory Registration and Medical Device Establishment License)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; Industrial Development Administration, MOEA; municipal government Economic Development Department; Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Ministry of Health and Welfare
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the MOEA registration certificate, automatically obtain the unified business number and complete business tax and profit-seeking enterprise income tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau, and file as a withholding taxpayer for salaried employees. If manufacturing premises are used, apply for a factory registration certificate with the municipal industrial authority under the Factory Management Act, submitting the factory layout, building safety certificate, and fire safety equipment list. Separately apply to TFDA for a Medical Device Manufacturer and Distributor License by submitting an establishment notice, quality management documentation, product technology dossier, sterilization data for the drug-eluting stent, and a cleanroom facility qualification certificate. The TFDA GMP license is a special manufacturing permit and commercial manufacture cannot begin before completion of a pre-licensing inspection.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate and unified business number
Factory building use permit and fire safety certificate
Factory layout drawing and equipment list
Medical device establishment license application to TFDA
QMS/GMP quality manual and corrective action procedure
Product-specific technical documentation including drug-elution coating validation
Environmental approval or registration certificate
Civil defense fire inspection certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau flags inconsistency between capital and expenditure, submit the CPA reconciliation and amended returns; for factory registration, address the municipal department's comments on building and fire safety within 30 calendar days; for TFDA GMP inspection deficiencies, submit a corrective and preventive action plan and request re-inspection within 60 days; if environmental registration is challenged, consult an environmental attorney and file an EIA report or mitigation plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA); Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Ministry of Health and Welfare; local municipal government Economic Development Department for factory registration and civil defense inspections
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing License (QMS/GMP Certificate) under the Medical Devices Act; Factory Registration Certificate under the Factory Management Act; Product License for Drug-Eluting Coronary Stent if marketed in Taiwan

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Taiwan), formerly Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Mandatory environmental licensing as a classified factory; for ISIC 3250 manufacturing with organic solvents, radioactive or hazardous waste handling, and effluent discharge, the project falls under Category B requiring an initial EIA report and review if the production capacity or solvent storage exceeds the Annex thresholds; otherwise, at minimum an Environmental Registration Certificate must be obtained before operation, and it is a precondition for water discharge, air pollutant and hazardous waste permits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Taiwan effluent standards for manufacturing premises: pH 6.0-9.0, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) not exceeding 30 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand (COD) not exceeding 100 mg/L, suspended solids (SS) not exceeding 30 mg/L, and applicable heavy metal limits for lead, chromium and other regulated substances. Coating and drug-elution solvent exhaust must meet the stationary source VOC emission standards, with a mandatory VOC removal efficiency of at least 90 percent where solvent consumption exceeds 10 metric tons per year, and fugitive VOC leaks from storage tanks and reactors must be controlled through a leak detection and repair program. Hazardous waste from solvent recovery and chemical residue must be stored in sealed containers, labeled, manifested, transported by licensed carriers and disposed of at a legally permitted treatment facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate and annual maintenance certificate under the Fire Services Act, covering automatic fire alarms, sprinklers, emergency lighting, fire extinguishers and escape routes; building use permit and structural loading certification issued by a registered architect or civil engineer; occupational safety and hygiene clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act covering hazardous chemical storage, machine guarding, lockout/tag-out, ventilation, electrostatic grounding, personal protective equipment, exposure monitoring and medical examination protocols for cleanroom workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan), acting through its regional tax administrations; online electronic portal: the Ministry of Finance Tax e-Service portal and the E-Invoice Service Platform for electronic uniform invoice transmission and VAT filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Taiwan WFOE (foreign-owned limited liability company): (1) obtain foreign investment approval from the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) under the Foreign Investment Act; (2) complete company incorporation and obtain the 8-digit Uniform Business Number (UBI) from MOEA, which is the same number used as the tax ID/VAT ID; (3) within the statutory period after commencement of business, file tax registration with the competent regional National Taxation Administration using the business/enterprise tax registration procedure available through the MOF Tax e-Service portal, and appoint a Taiwan-based tax representative and registered place of business; (4) register as a Uniform Invoice user and, if required, enroll in the electronic invoice service through a certified service provider or the MOF E-Invoice platform. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a Taiwan fixed place of business that merely earns Taiwan-source income should obtain a withholding tax identification number through the withholding statement registration process; however, that number is not a VAT registration ID and does not permit input VAT credit recovery.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Taiwan WFOE is a separate tax-resident profit-seeking enterprise subject to corporate income tax on its worldwide income, and its foreign shareholder is separately subject to Taiwan-source dividend withholding or treaty relief, if applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Taiwan does not have a U.S.-style check-the-box election or a hybrid-mismatch entity election. The Anti-Tax Avoidance Rules and general anti-avoidance doctrines may recharacterize transactions, but a WFOE cannot elect pass-through treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Business Tax (value-added tax / VAT) under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act (Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$200,000 average monthly taxable sales for goods and NT$100,000 for services, as prescribed under the Business Tax Act and Ministry of Finance threshold directives; once exceeded, the business is a compulsory VAT-registered Uniform Invoice taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registered businesses must issue Uniform Invoices for each taxable sale. Where electronic Uniform Invoices (e-Invoices) are used, the invoice data is transmitted digitally to the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Service Platform through certified e-invoice service providers or the MOF turnkey gateway, and is reconciled with the bi-monthly Business Tax return due by the 15th day after each two-month filing period. There is no per-transaction real-time fiscal stamp for every general VAT taxpayer, but the E-Invoice Platform performs automated validation, storage and anti-fraud verification; invoice serial numbers and digital signatures must be valid, and any abnormality or misuse of e-invoice numbers is subject to immediate blocking, rectification orders and penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, sales of goods physically exported from Taiwan are zero-rated for VAT; for a Class III medical device stent manufacturer, the zero-rate applies when the goods are sold to a foreign buyer and the export is evidenced by a Customs export declaration. Services used or consumed wholly outside Taiwan and for which proceeds are received in foreign currency may also qualify as zero-rated exports if the statutory supporting documents are kept.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice and zero-rated export sales invoice
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or packers receipt for consolidated shipments)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-exchange settlement certificate showing repatriation of export proceeds
Letter of Credit, SWIFT wire, or export contract and payment statement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Administration cross-checks zero-rated export turnover against the Customs Administration export declarations, E-Invoice Platform records and inward foreign exchange receipts. Where zero-rating is not substantiated by the mandatory customs and FX documentation, the output VAT is clawed back at 5% from the original reporting period, late-payment surcharge is assessed, and a statutory penalty of up to five times the evaded tax may be imposed under the Business Tax Act; fraudulent e-invoice or false export documentation may also trigger criminal liability under the Tax Collection Act and suspension of the business registration. The tax authority may re-open completed periods for fraud and concealment within the extended assessment period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC / 中国人民银行) is the sovereign central bank of the People's Republic of China, exercising authority over monetary policy, financial stability, and systemic liquidity. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE / 国家外汇管理局), administered under the PBOC, is the exclusive delegated foreign-exchange (FX) regulatory organ governing all onshore CNY convertibility, cross-border capital flows, trade-in-goods settlement, FDI capital account registration, export proceeds supervision, and onshore FX hedging transactions for the CN_WFOE_LTD. SAFE operates through regional branches (e.g., Beijing branch, Shanghai head-office service window) and has delegated registration and verification authority to designated designated banks (外汇指定银行), subject to ex post facto audit on a risk-tier basis. For the Taiwan-investor leg, the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC / 中央銀行, Taipei) administers all New Taiwan Dollar (TWD) monetary and FX policy, including TWD/CNY clearing under the Cross-Strait Currency Clearing Collaboration Framework Memorandum (两岸货币清算合作备忘录) signed on 31 August 2012. Under that framework, Bank of China's Taipei branch (中国银行台北分行) acts as the CNY clearing bank for Taiwan-side RMB settlement, and CTBC Bank's Shanghai branch (中国信託商業銀行上海分行) acts as the TWD clearing bank for mainland-side TWD settlement. The WFOE, as a PRC legal entity, is subject to PBOC/SAFE jurisdiction for all onshore FX activity; the Taiwan parent is subject to CBC's foreign-currency position reporting and outward remittance monitoring requirements under Taiwan's Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (管理外匯條例). Cross-strait payments must observe the documentation standards of both regulators and the Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) financial-service annexes to the extent applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed, non-fully-convertible currency regime with a fundamental legal bifurcation between the current account (经常项目) and the capital account (资本项目). Current account (goods, services, profit remittance, interest, royalties, and travel) is functionally convertible for bona fide transactions; the RMB is freely settleable for import of raw materials (e.g., nitinol alloy tubing, cobalt-chromium sheet stock, bioresorbable poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) polymer resin, sirolimus/everolimus/paclitaxel drug substances, PTFE hydrophilic coatings) and export proceeds from finished coronary drug-eluting stents, subject to SAFE authenticity verification (真实性审核) that requires the presenting bank to match the submitted commercial invoice, customs declaration, transport documents, and purchase/sales contract. No pre-approval from SAFE is required for current-account items, but each transaction must be reported within 5 working days through the bank's Administration of Foreign Exchange for Trade in Goods system (货物贸易外汇监测系统) and the International Transactions Reporting System (收支申报). Capital account (FDI capital injection, cross-border loans, equity acquisition of domestic enterprises, outbound investment, securities investment, and real-estate investments) remains heavily restricted and requires: (i) SAFE FDI registration (外汇登记), (ii) opening of a capital account (资本金账户) at a designated bank, (iii) external-debt registration (外债登记) if any cross-border loan facility is used, and (iv) compliance with the Foreign Investment Negative List (外商投资准入特别管理措施（负面清单）2024 version) to ensure the medical-device manufacturing scope is in a permitted category; Class III vascular intervention devices are not on the negative list, hence 100% Taiwan-owned capital is permissible. Profit and dividend remittance to the Taiwan parent is permitted on the current account, but the bank and SAFE will demand (i) a valid audit report of the WFOE's statutory financial statements issued by a Chinese CPA firm, (ii) the shareholders' resolution for dividend distribution approved by the board, (iii) a certificate of tax settlement including corporate income tax (CIT) payment and the 10% dividend withholding tax under the Cross-Strait Taxation Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Tax Evasion on Income Tax (海峽兩岸避免雙重課稅及加強稅務合作協議);. if the Taiwan shareholder is a natural person or is deemed a Taiwan tax resident with a certificate of residence, the reduced 5% dividend withholding rate may apply on application; otherwise 10% applies; (iv) a SAFE Form I (基础信息登记表) and Form III (境外汇出申请书) signed by the legal representative; and (v) the bank's assessment that profits arose from operations rather than from capital revaluation or unrealized gains. Principal repayment out of the WFOE's registered capital is not permitted; any capital reduction or deregistration requires SAFE approval and a public notice through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (信用公示系统) with a 45-day creditor-opposition window, and the Taiwan parent must redeem its interest at fair market valuation with FDI deregistration; funds can only leave after a formal reduction of registered capital is recorded with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and tax clearance from the tax authorities is obtained. In practice, FBME cross-border RMB settlement is also available under the Cross-border RMB Business measures (跨境人民币结算业务管理暂行办法, PBOC 2009) for both current and capital account items, with the advantage of bypassing some FX conversion constraints; the WFOE should evaluate a dual-currency treasury (USD and RMB) to maximize remittance efficiency. Overall hurdle severity: MEDIUM-HIGH for capital account; LOW-MEDIUM for current account; the company must designate a treasury manager to ensure every incoming/outgoing current-account item is matched to an underlying bona fide transaction and every capital-account item is pre-registered.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China formally abolished mandatory export proceeds surrender (强制结汇) for the corporate sector in October 2012 under SAFE Circular Huifa [2012] No. 38 (国家外汇管理局关于优化货物贸易外汇管理方式的通知), and the rule was reconfirmed under SAFE Huifa [2020] No. 14 (国家外汇管理局关于进一步推进外汇管理改革完善真实合规性审核的通知). The CN_WFOE_LTD is therefore entitled to retain 100% of its export proceeds from coronary drug-eluting stents in a foreign currency operational account (经常项目外汇账户) at a designated bank, and has the right — not the obligation — to voluntarily settle into CNY at the market rate. However, SAFE imposes mandatory administrative duties on the exporter: (1) Declaration and Registration: all exports must be reported to the China Customs through the 'Single Window' (单一窗口) before departure, and each consignment's foreign-currency receipt must be linked to the customs declaration number through the Trade Monitoring System (货物贸易外汇监测系统); actual collection must be registered within 30 calendar days after the customs declaration date (出口收汇日期核销期). (2) Export Proceeds Cascade: when wires from overseas distributors (e.g., US/EU hospital procurement frameworks, Taiwan-licensed distributers, Southeast Asian importers) arrive in the WFOE's settlement account, the bank will perform an automatic matching with the customs declaration record; no separate 'surrender' is required, but the company must maintain an export proceeds verification logbook and produce it on SAFE audit at least every three years; medical device exports (HS 9021.39, vascular stents; HS 9018.39 for related catheters) do not require prior SAFE approval, but they do require the export license endorsement under the PRC Export Control Law (出口管制法) where applicable; Class III devices must also bear the NMPA registration certificate number on the customs declaration; exports to Taiwan are treated as cross-strait trade and must conform to the ECFA early-harvest lists for product tariffs and the cross-strait Goods Trade Agreement procedures where applicable. (3) Reconciliation and Tolerance Bands: if actual FX received deviates from the export declaration amount by more than 5% of the FOB value, or if the timing of receipt exceeds 90 days after export without a bank-approved extension, the WFOE will be reclassified by SAFE to (i) Class B (B类), subjecting it to 100% document checking for one year and mandatory on-site entry-exit verification for every single transaction; or (ii) Class C (C类), which effectively imposes prior-verified payment restrictions and may require a full compliance review by the FX administration. (4) Conversion: voluntary settlement proceeds from the operational FX account are freely usable for CNY operating expenditure, including payroll, raw-material purchasing, utility, and tax payments, but cannot be placed into a capital-account item unless settled through the capital account rules. (5) Annual SAFE Verification: annually, the WFOE must complete the SAFE 'Foreign Exchange Revenue and Expenditure for Trade' annual verification (外汇收支申报年度報告) and ensure the bank's 'Unit of Foreign Exchange Revenue and Expenditure Goods Trade' (货物贸易外汇收支企业名录) listing is current; revocation from the Directory would suspend all export settlement for 1–3 months. Additional rules under the capital-account deference regime: if the WFOE receives a remittance that exceeds RMB 500,000 per transaction and it fails to clear within 10 working days of the customs declaration, the bank will flag it; if the company holds foreign currency in excess of its verified annual business volume (based on the previous year's declarations), it must either settle it or apply for a quota increase. Effective compliance with surrender-related monitoring is a material precondition for the successful opening and continuous operation of the corporate bank accounts and for the company's ability to access the expedited FX 'green channel' offered to High-tier medical exporters.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW as a primary onshore treasury rail; MEDIUM as an ancillary offshore collection/settlement overlay for the WFOE's overseas distributors, with strict legal constraints. The China regulatory framework does not recognize offshore digital EMI licenses (e.g., UK FCA or US MSB or Singapore MAS Major Payment Institution) as valid authorization to conduct payment services in mainland China. Under the PBOC Administrative Measures for the Payment Services Provided by Non-Financial Institutions (非金融机构支付服务管理办法, PBOC Decree [2010] No. 2, as amended), the CFCA (China's non-bank payment license) is the sole gateway for a private entity to process RMB payments; the WFOE cannot use an offshore EMI portal (Airwallex, Revolut Business, Payoneer, WorldFirst, Currenxie, PingPong's cross-border card) to initiate onshore RMB debits, receive export proceeds in CNY, or settle trade invoices with domestic suppliers, because the onshore bank receiving the funds must match the SAFE trade declarations to the actual FX flow, and any layering through an unlicensed intermediary would be considered an unauthorized payment channel (非法支付渠道) under Article 11 of the Non-financial Institution Payment Measures and Article 221 of the Criminal Law concerning illegal business activities (非法经营罪). As a supplementary instrument, the WFOE may use an offshore EMI platform to collect USD/EUR/GBP payments from foreign hospital or distributor buyers into a virtual multi-currency account, and then sweep the aggregate balance into the onshore BOC or CMB Operational FX Account via the FX remittance (汇入汇款) rail, with each individual invoice documented on SAFE's trade-monitoring portal before the sweep; this pattern must preserve entity-of-record integrity (i.e., the bank account in the WFOE's own name at the EMI is permissible as a collection account, but not as an onshore settlement account). The Fintech EMIs' remote onboarding convenience is counterbalanced by the High_Risk_Special_License underwriting standard imposed by Chinese banks on Class III medical device manufacturers: the onshore bank will refuse to accept a 'trust-me-on-PDF' dossier and will require an in-person interview and physical inspection regardless of the parent's EMI history. Additionally, the Taiwan parent may, for its own cross-border RMB collection from mainland customers, use the cross-border RMB payment system via CTBC or First Commercial Bank (Taiwan), but the China WFOE cannot rely on any Taiwan-regulated EMI (e.g., 街口支付 or TNG) for its mainland outbound payments. Conclusion: the WFOE's primary clearing rail must be a licensed Chinese Tier-1 bank; offshore EMIs may serve only as a front-end receivable collection gateway for remote overseas clients, and even then only where the WFOE confirms full regulatory documentation, maintains a formal outsourcing agreement, and obtains the bank's prior written acknowledgment that it will not process any RMB conversion or settlement activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Full physical presence and on-site KYC interview are mandatory for the CN_WFOE_LTD under PRC banking regulations; no end-to-end remote account opening is permitted for a corporate account. Concretely: (1) The legal representative (法定代表人) of the WFOE, whether the Taiwan parent's designated director or a mainland-resident GM, must appear physically at the bank branch at the time of application, with original passport or Mainland Travel Permit for Taiwan Residents (台湾居民往来大陆通行证 / 台胞证), and must answer a compliance interview administered by the bank's senior compliance officer. If the legal representative cannot appear, the bank may accept a notarized irrevocable power of attorney (授权委托书) granting the GM or a senior finance officer the authority to open the account, but the bank's compliance team will still conduct a video conference and require an in-person meeting during the on-site inspection phase; (2) The bank's KYC team will perform a physical site visit to the NMPA-registered manufacturing facility, verify laser micro-machining clean room equipment, check the presence of the Class III medical device production license on the wall, take photographs of the production line, and confirm that the registered office address matches the business license; if the facility is a virtual or leased co-working space without production evidence, the account application is automatically rejected under the bank's high-risk industry protocol (高风险行业敏感名单); (3) For the Taiwan investor, the bank requires the Taiwan parent's original certificate of incorporation (公司登記證明書), the notarized and legalized Board Resolution authorizing the investment and the bank signatories, the latest audited financial statements (preferably with capital account history), the passport copies and power-of-attorney certificates of each beneficial owner holding ≥25% (PBOC beneficial owner rule), and, where the Taiwan parent is a listed company, its latest annual report or public prospectus; (4) Additional interview topics include the precise description of the stent manufacturing process (laser cutting, electropolishing, drug coating, sterilization), the sales distribution channels (original equipment manufacturer (OEM) vs. own-brand international distribution), the expected monthly transaction volume and frequency, the purpose of each account, the source of the initial capital injection, the identity of ultimate beneficial owners down to the natural-person level, and confirmation that no PEP (politically exposed person) or sanctions nexus exists; (5) The bank will require the account to be funded by the Taiwan parent's wire after the account documentation is fully executed; the first wire will trigger an automated alert and a second compliance check; the bank will not permit the WFOE to move funds out until the SAFE FDI registration and the capital verification report (验资报告) are produced; (6) All seized bank seals (公章, 财务专用章, 法定代表人名章) must be carved at the bank's approved supplier and registered at the local public security bureau (公安局) - this step cannot be delegated digitally; (7) A mandatory board resolution is required for the opening of the Capital Escrow Account and again for any operational account that will receive export proceeds, specifying the account's designated purpose, signatory authorization limits (e.g., any wire over RMB 500,000 requires two signatures), and the dual-signatory matrix in the case of a Taiwan-based CFO as second approver; (8) The New Measures on 'Simplified Account Opening for Foreign-Invested Enterprises' in Shanghai Pilot Free Trade Zone and the Hainan Free Trade Port allow some electronic pre-filing, but the final wet signature and physical presence remain non-waivable for a Class III med-tech WFOE under the code 'High_Risk_Special_License'; the bank will not depart from this rule because of the issuer's own AML risk rating (industry subclass: Healthcare Device - Special License - AML high-risk under the China Anti-Money Laundering Law (2006, revised 2022) Article 2(1) and the 2021 AML Administrative Provisions for Payment Institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait beneficial ownership opacity: the Taiwan parent's ultimate natural-person controllers are not visible from the PRC business license; the bank flags a potential hidden controller (隐名股东), a trust/private foundation overlay, or a nominee shareholding arrangement, and the risk of the WFOE being used as a round-trip investment vehicle (返程投资) is elevated under SAFE binary tracking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a parallel documentation stack in both Chinese and English: (i) the Taiwan parent's Certificate of Incorporation (公司登記證明書) and the most recent year's share register (股東名簿) evidencing all shareholders holding ≥1% of issued shares; (ii) a natural-person-level ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration form (实际受益人申报表) prepared in accordance with PBOC Document Yinfa [2018] No. 168 (关于加强反洗钱客户身份识别有关工作的通知) Section III, enumerating each natural person owning ≥10% of equity/voting rights and providing passport copies, residential proof, and source of wealth; (iii) a graphical corporate chain map showing the Taiwan parent to the CN_WFOE_LTD with all intermediate entities, including any Cayman, BVI, or Hong Kong holding vehicles; (iv) a legal opinion from a PRC-qualified law firm analyzing the actual controller determination under the PRC Company Law (2023 Amendment) Articles 180 and 265, and a notarized affidavit from the Taiwan parent's board confirming no nominee/代持 arrangements within the meaning of the PRC Foreign Investment Law Article 28; (v) proof of filing the annual foreign-investment information report (外商投资信息报告年度报告) with the MOFCOM, including the UBO page; (vi) the WFOE's Articles of Association with the authorized signatory and voting structure; (vii) a bank statement of the Taiwan parent for the past 12 months demonstrating the source of the capital injection was operational profits, not third-party financing; and (viii) a signed irrevocable letter of acknowledgement from the Taiwan parent accepting liability for any false declaration, plus a comfort letter from a Taipei-based law firm confirming the absence of statutory nominee ownership rules under Taiwan Company Law Article 12 (as amended).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidence_defense_note: The bank will likely request a supplementary interview with the Taiwan parent's CFO to map the family tree and confirm no undisclosed tightening; prepare a scripted presentation and have the CFO carry original corporate minute books.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Class III medical device licensing integrity: the bank's automated underwriting flags the NMPA device classification, demanding proof that the WFOE holds the specific production license for 'coronary drug-eluting stent system' and that the product's NMPA registration number is not suspended, revoked, or sham; the bank also tests for unauthorized repackaging or contract manufacturing (贴牌/OEM) without a valid commissioned manufacturing record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) the original NMPA Medical Device Manufacturing License (医疗器械生产许可证, Class III) with the license number and product scope line item '冠状动脉药物洗脱支架系统', issued by the NMPA; (ii) the current NMPA Medical Device Registration Certificate (医疗器械注册证) (e.g., 国械注准20223750888) with the appendix schedule listing the stent model names, delivery system diameters, and drug-eluting dose; (iii) the ISO 13485:2016 Certificate from a recognized conformity assessment body (TÜV Rheinland or BSI) covering the company's full quality management system at the production site; (iv) the ISO 10993 Biological Evaluation battery reports (ISO 10993-1, 10993-3, 10993-4, 10993-5, 10993-7, 10993-9, 10993-10, 10993-11) for the final device, plus the ISO 11137 sterilization validation certificate; (v) the latest provincial drug administration (省级药品监督管理局) GMP inspection certificate and the inspection report no. 202X-XXXXX, dated within the prior 12 months; (vi) the product's Certificate of Analysis (CoA) for the most recent production batch, together with the release documentation showing the batch was distributed for the Chinese and export markets; (vii) a list of all states/distributors for contract-manufacturing arrangements, each with a licensed Code/授权制造/代工合同 connecting the WFOE's production to the registered device; (viii) a consent from the NMPA that the intended Taiwan sales via a Taiwan distributor (or the Taiwan parent's separate Taiwan marketing license under Taiwan's Medical Devices Administration Act / 醫療器材管理法) does not require an additional site-file amendment to the mainland production license; and (ix) a memorandum from the PRC regulatory counsel mapping the license hierarchy under the PRC Medical Device Supervision and Administration Regulations (State Council Order No. 739) and its 2021 implementation regulations to demonstrate full compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export-control and anti-embargo compliance: the bank flags the presence of advanced drug-eluting technology and micro-manufacturing for implants as a potential dual-use/national-security-export item, particularly the risk that the WFOE's end users might include OFAC/SDN-listed hospitals or procurement agents in Crimea, Iran, Syria, North Korea, or entities on the US Entity List for Chinese MedTech; the bank's screening engine will search for adverse media and sanctions connections on both the Taiwan parent and the WFOE's commercial counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble: (i) a comprehensive transactional Sanctions & PEP Screening Log generated from a reputable automated engine (Refinitiv World-Check, LexisNexis Bridger Insight XG, or Dow Jones Risk & Compliance) covering every bank counterparty, supplier, distributor, and ultimate hospital buyer for the prior 36 months; (ii) a signed End-User/End-Use Certificate (最终用户和最终用途证明) for each export sale, each bearing the purchaser's official letterhead, the specific purchase order number, the medical facility's registration number in its home state, and the explicit statement that the device will only be implanted by licensed physicians in a licensed hospital and will not be re-exported, resold, or transferred to any third party without the exporter's consent; (iii) an Export Control Classification Matrix for the device and raw materials, showing whether each is controlled under the PRC Export Control Law (出口管制法) Category 1 (national security), Category 2 (dual-use), or uncontrolled 'EAR99' under the US Export Administration Regulations; any controlled element must have a valid PRC dual-use export license number; (iv) a Taiwan Customs/Taipei-based goods re-export certificate from the Bureau of Foreign Trade (MOEA) demonstrating that the Taiwan parent's imported input materials (e.g., cobalt-chromium alloy L605, nitinol tubing, PLLA resins) were lawfully imported with no re-export restriction and subject to no US/EU re-export condition from the original manufacturer; (v) a Board-approved Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) and UK Bribery Act 2010 Compliance Policy, together with training attendance records for all senior personnel; (vi) anti-bribery contractual clauses incorporated in all distributor agreements, prohibiting corrupt payments to any public hospital administrator; (vii) a legal opinion from PRC trade-control counsel confirming that the specific geometry/features of the drug-eluting stent do not fall under the PRC 'Sensitive Items and Technologies Export Control List' and that the import of the drug substance (sirolimus/everolimus) is lawful under the PRC pharmacopeia and Custom import license schemes; and (viii) a copy of the WFOE's 'Enterprise Foreign Trade Operator' record (对外贸易经营者备案登记表) and the previous 12 months' export license batch records with China Customs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party transfer pricing distortion: the WFOE imports polymer and drug substances from the Taiwan parent (or a TW sister company), exports finished stents to the Taiwan parent's trading subsidiary in Hong Kong or directly to a Taiwan distributor, and pays technology royalties to the Taiwan parent; bank compliance ascertains that such related-party flows may be disguised profit repatriation or capital flight, and would impair the bank's obligation to report unusual FX flows to SAFE (e.g., under the Classification for Unusual FX Outflows).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) contemporaneous Transfer Pricing Dossier (同期资料) under SAT Public Announcement [2016] No. 42, consisting of a Local File (本地文档), a Master File (主体文档) if the group turnover exceeds RMB 1 billion, and a Special File (特殊事项文档) where the WFOE's related-party transaction exceeds RMB 40 million in trade or RMB 20 million in royalties; (ii) the intercompany supply agreement for the raw materials with a pricing methodology based on the arm's-length CUP (comparable uncontrolled price) method, including a benchmarking study obtained from a recognized database (e.g., RoyaltyStat or TP Catalyst) showing the royalty rate does not exceed 1.5% of net sales for the stent technology; (iii) a functional, asset, and risk (FAR) analysis demonstrating that the WFOE bears the full manufacturing, quality, regulatory, credit, and inventory risk, while the Taiwan parent performs only treasury, brand, and (limited) sales-coordination functions; (iv) for the finished-good sale to the Hong Kong or Taiwan trading entity, a second benchmarking analysis using the cost-plus method or resale-price method with a cross-check commending that the remunerated margin for the WFOE is within the interquartile range of comparable medical-device contract manufacturers, typically 20-30% EBIT; (v) the approved intercompany services agreement for the R&D and IP license, with the fee schedule based on allocation keys and prior-year tax filing proof; (vi) the annual related-party transaction schedule (关联业务往来报告表) submitted to the PRC tax authorities in the A400 series forms for the current tax year; (vii) a prior three-year PRC CIT settlement certificate (企业所得税汇算清缴) from the tax bureau as evidence of full tax payment and no loss-carryforward abuse; (viii) a memorandum from a Big-4 TP expert summarizing that the PRC tax authority, in a contemporaneous TP risk assessment for Class III medical-device makers, would find the transfer pricing documentation as providing exemption from the 10%-em markup-related penalty; (ix) copies of the bank's previous FX settlement records for these related-party items proving that SAFE had accepted the PO/invoice documentation in the prior period without any violation.
